LESSON: TEMPERATURE

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: MEASUREMENTS
Topic 3.6: Temperature
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Temperature, part of MEASUREMENTS in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: when dealing with hot substances) 1. How does temperature affect our everyday lives? 2. How do we measure temperature?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Temperature together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: A learner develops teamwork as they work in groups and use tools of measuring

temperature.

43

● Digital literacy: A learner develops interaction with technology as they determine the temperature of different places using

digital devices.

Values:
● Responsibility: A learner enhances diligence and excellence as they carefully handle tools of measuring temperature.

● Integrity: A learner enhances accountability as they give correct measurements of temperature.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Self-awareness: A learner takes their body temperatures.

● Safety and security: A learner works in a group and exercises caution when dealing with hot substances.

Link to other subjects:

● Integrated Science: A learner considers body temperatures to establish their health status and dressing appropriately.

● Social Studies: A learner considers climatic temperature changes.

Suggested Learning Resources:

● Thermometers, Digital Talking Thermometers, Cards, Thermometers, digital devices with assistive technology such as

screen magnifiers, Print and Braille Course Book.
